cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Steer the Suspicion
cards.instruction: Hide your responsibility by redirecting every new clue toward a safer explanation before anyone can connect it back to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write to the manufacturer. Your shelf fell because they supplied the wrong bracket.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You fitted it upside down. Look at the arrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll complain about the arrow. I'll hold it while you photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew that arrow. I watched you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Photograph both sides, then. I'll put in the complaint that they made us draw our own safety markings.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads manufacturer complaint; A3 changes target to the arrow and offers holding help; A5 turns A own marking into manufacturer failure while retaining B photography.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 hold it follows arrow, but the object to hold is the bracket bearing the arrow; name it rather than require a physical inference.

relationship.evidence: B2 identifies upside-down fitting and B4 witnessed A draw the mark, both relevant evidence.

heightening.evidence: B4 ownership of the mark causes A5 to blame missing factory markings and request both sides documented.

specificity.evidence: A1 fallen shelf and bracket are clear, but A3 dangling object makes the proposed helpful action less clear than necessary.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 can say hold the bracket while you photograph it in place of the vague hold it while you photograph.
